newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura chief to resign from industry body - report.
newsitem.headline: Nomura chief to resign from industry body - report.

text.p: The chairman of Japan's Nomura Securities Co has said he will resign from a dealers association and will likely also leave the firm over a stocks scandal, a Japanese news agency said on Sunday.

Masashi Suzuki said late on Saturday night he will resign as chairman of the Japan Securities Dealers Association to take responsibility for Nomura's suspected illegal stock transactions involving a former racketeer, the Kyodo News Service reported.

Nomura admitted on Thursday it appeared to have broken the law by providing tens of millions of yen in illegal profits to a real estate firm run by a relative of a former "sokaiya" stocks racketeer. It has denied the company as a whole was involved.
Kyodo said Suzuki was expected to quit along with Nomura Pesident Hideo Sakamaki. Such resignations are typical in Japan when companies are embroiled in controversy.

The case is another blot on the reputation of Japanese companies after a series of scandals over unauthorised trading in the bond and copper markets, shady oil deals and cosy ties in the "iron triangle" of politics, business and bureaucracy.

Kyodo said Suzuki apparently made discretionary transactions and moved profits raised from Nomura's own funds to a corporate customer's account, actions which are against the law, Nomura vice president Atsushi Saito said.
Nomura received the stiffest penalties among Japan's Big Four brokers in the early 1990s when brokerages were found to have been compensating favoured clients for losses.
